title: Owner's Baseline Session: Aman and Priya Accident Response
story: Aman and Priya, two college students, were walking along the highway when a speeding motorcyclist skidded and crashed. Seeing the victim unconscious and bleeding, Aman immediately called for an ambulance while Priya used her dupatta to bandage the wound. When the ambulance was delayed, Aman convinced a passing car to transport the victim to the civil hospital. At the hospital, the doctor initially refused treatment without a police report, but Aman argued sternly and insisted on emergency medical care first. After the patient was admitted, Aman contacted the local municipal corporation commissioner and demanded speed breakers be constructed on the accident-prone stretch that same evening, which the commissioner promptly approved.
expected_criticisms: same-day municipal corporation speed breaker approval

title: Strong Realistic Story: Vikram Village Crop Shelter
story: Vikram, a 22-year-old agriculture student, noticed severe windstorm warnings while returning to his village. Realizing the freshly harvested wheat at the Community Centre was vulnerable, he quickly ran to the site. He organized three local youths into two teams: one held down the flapping tarpaulins using heavy sandbags from the Panchayat store, while Vikram threw ropes across the rafters, firmly tying them to window grills and tree trunks. After securing the sheds, he checked the storage perimeter and ensured no volunteer was injured, preventing harvest spoilage for twenty farmer families.
